titleStmt.author: Andrew M. Guess
Jonathan Nagler
Joshua A. Tucker

bibl.title: Less than you think: Prevalence and predictors of fake news dissemination on Facebook

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: who actually posted links from fake news domains to their Facebook friends during the 2016 US campaign, measured from profile data rather than from what people say they did
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: how common fake news sharing was, and which individual characteristics predict it once ideology, partisanship, education and overall posting volume are held constant
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a survey of 3500 linked to 1191 respondents' real Facebook sharing: over 90% shared no fake news at all, conservatives shared more, and the oldest group shared nearly seven times as much as the youngest with everything else held constant
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: existence
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the dissemination of deliberately false political content by ordinary users - rare, concentrated, and predicted by age more robustly than by anything else measured
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a three-wave YouGov panel linked by consent to Facebook timeline data, with posted domains cross-referenced against journalist- and academic-built lists of fake news publishers, modelled as counts by quasi-Poisson regression with sample-matching weights
span.term: a three-wave YouGov panel linked by consent to Facebook timeline data, with posted domains cross-referenced against journalist- and academic-built lists of fake news publishers, modelled as counts by quasi-Poisson regression with sample-matching weights
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: BuzzSumo ranks domains by Facebook engagement; a journalist checks each for the hallmark features of a fake news site - no contact page, syndicated content, recently registered; a supervised classifier trained on 7 million pages removes anything it calls hard news. Thirty domains become twenty-one, and every share in the dependent variable is a link to one of those twenty-one
span.term: a category built by three procedures in sequence
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: linking profile data to a survey removes the self-report bias in what people say they shared, and it cannot recover what they thought they were sharing. The design buys accuracy about the act and gives up access to the state of mind - which is the quantity the survey experiments measure and cannot observe the act of
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: 3500 respondents, 1331 consenting to share profile data, 1191 successfully linked - and the linked respondents were more knowledgeable and more politically engaged than those who declined. The behavioural half of the design is available only from people willing to hand it over, and willingness correlates with the subject matter
span.term: a consent gradient inside the sample
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: sharing is a choice made over what arrived. Without the News Feed, a group that shares more fake news may be a group that saw more of it, and no amount of control for the sharer's characteristics separates the two. The authors state this rather than resolving it
span.term: the unobserved half of every social media finding
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: there is no measure of whether respondents knew that what they shared was false
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the data are observational and cannot provide causal evidence, and an omitted variable cannot be definitively ruled out
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: half the respondents with Facebook accounts declined to share their profile data, and the linked ones were more knowledgeable and politically engaged
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the composition of respondents' News Feeds is unobserved, so exposure cannot be separated from willingness to share
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: posts deleted before consent are invisible, and the authors argue rather than measure that this should reduce noise rather than bias
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the conservative finding is sensitive to coding and rests on a small number of respondents
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the ideological pattern may reflect the pro-Trump slant of the available content and the ordinary tendency to share what one agrees with, rather than a greater propensity to share falsehood
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: there is no commonly accepted ground-truth standard for what counts as fake news, so the dependent variable rests on lists built by journalists and academics
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: digital trace data linked to survey response, carried from computational social science into a question political science had been answering with self-report
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a supervised text classifier from information retrieval, used not to make the finding but to draw the boundary of the outcome variable
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the total number of links shared of any kind reported beside the fake news count, and included as a covariate in every model
span.note: eliminates: a low fake-news count meaning people do not share links - most respondents shared hundreds, so the rarity is about the content · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the relationship between overall sharing volume and fake news sharing examined directly, rather than only controlled for
span.note: eliminates: the explanation that some respondents will share anything - the heaviest sharers shared LESS fake news, which is the opposite of that prediction · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the same model applied to hard news sharing as a placebo outcome
span.note: eliminates: age predicting online sharing in general - if it did, the predictors of hard news would look the same, and they do not include age at all · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: five different lists of fake news domains, including one built from 948 individual fact-checks and one crowdsourced, with the analysis rerun on each
span.note: eliminates: one journalist's list carrying the finding - the category has no ground truth, so the robustness has to be to the choice of vocabulary itself · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: an exact-URL variant of the analysis using only the 948 fact-checked stories, rather than counting every article from a listed domain
span.note: eliminates: the assumption that everything published by a fake news domain is fake - the stricter definition does not need it · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: hard news domains removed from the list by a classifier trained on 7 million shared pages, so that hyperpartisan sites are excluded from the outcome
span.note: eliminates: the contested hyperpartisan category being counted as fake news, which would make an ideological finding partly definitional · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: negative binomial and OLS models run alongside the quasi-Poisson, with the quasi-Poisson chosen by a dispersion test
span.note: eliminates: the count model's distributional assumptions producing the result · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: ideology and party identification, correlated at r = 0.31, entered separately and together, with all three specifications reported
span.note: eliminates: a collinearity decision being made silently in the authors' favour - they name the correlation and publish every version · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the models re-fitted as negative binomial and OLS alongside the Poisson and quasi-Poisson specifications, with dispersion tests deciding between the latter two
span.note: eliminates: that the sharing result is an artefact of one count-model specification · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: respondents asked to check which categories of profile information they were willing to share, with no access to News Feeds or to friends' data
span.note: eliminates: collecting more than was consented to - the field-by-field opt-in bounds the data at the point of collection · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
